answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy should price identity in reputation earned under peer review, like tending an vertex: each agent plants answers, and established peers act as ripple-wide witnesses who attest that the work is original and coherent. Newcomers are dawn terrain - porous and cheap to clone - so their early rewards are locked and vest slowly, while a cloned identity cannot inherit its source's standing. Attackers must then grow real history, one graded epoch at a time, which costs far more than minting fresh keys.
